Grandpa's Clock

By A. Writer — Published March 3rd

Every evening, Grandpa would wind the old clock on the mantel. It had belonged to his father, and to his father's father before that, ticking through wars and weddings and quiet Sunday afternoons without ever once stopping.

Outside, the wind picked up, rattling the shutters and pulling dead leaves across the yard in long, restless spirals. Grandpa didn't seem to notice. He was listening to the clock instead, the way some people listen to rain.

"It keeps time better than I do," he used to say, tapping the glass face with one crooked finger. "Long after I'm gone, this clock will still be telling the truth about the hour."

Years later, when the house was finally sold, the new owners found the clock still running in the empty hallway, faithfully wound by whoever had come before, keeping the one promise that mattered.
